target.title: fix(mcp): fix-mcp-cli-oauth-login-timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw mcp login <name>` could see the OAuth login workflow hang indefinitely when the MCP server, OAuth discovery endpoint, or an upstream proxy stopped responding during the CLI login flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps the fix scoped to the explicit CLI OAuth login workflow by passing the configured MCP `requestTimeoutMs` from `mcp login` into `runMcpOAuthLogin(...)`, then wrapping the login-only `fetchFn` with a request deadline. That gives the login path a real HTTP timeout without widening this change to the broader MCP runtime transport layer.

## User Impact

Operators using `openclaw mcp login` now get bounded OAuth HTTP requests instead of a login command that can hang forever on a stalled remote endpoint. Existing configured MCP timeout values now apply to this login path as well.

## Evidence

Validated with focused tests:

```bash
pnpm test src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts
pnpm test src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Added coverage for:

- `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts`: `mcp login` forwards `resolved.requestTimeoutMs` as `fetchTimeoutMs`
- `src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts`: OAuth fetches abort with `TimeoutError` when the configured login timeout elapses
